newsitem.title: USA: FERC allows Pacific to withdraw filing.
newsitem.headline: FERC allows Pacific to withdraw filing.

text.p: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) approved Pacific Enterprise's (PE) request to cancel a rate schedule filing for a planned power marketing affiliate, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
PE sought to withdraw the filing for its Ensource unit as a boon to its argument that FERC does not have jurisdiction over the company's planned merger with Enova Corp.
Without a power marketing unit, PE believes FERC cannot hold that it is a public utility under the terms of the Federal Power Act.
Ensource will continue to operate as a natural gas marketer, the PE spokesman said.
FERC has not yet said whether it will declare jurisdiction and the two companies on Monday filed a back-up merger application with the federal regulatory agency.
PE, the parent of Southern California Gas Co and Enova, parent of San Diego Gas and Electric Co, announced in October plans to merge pending regulatory approvals.
The companies also plan to launch a pre-merger joint venture aimed at retail utility services.
